full_judgment:
Md Moinul Islam Chowdhury J: At the instance of the Defendant-Petitioner Mohammad Abdus Samad, this Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 10-11-2011 passed by the District Judge, Rangpur, in Civil Revision No. 42 of 2009 reversing the judgment and order dated 14-9-2009 passed by Assistant Judge, Badarganj Court, Rangpur, in Other suit No. 1032 of 2008 should not be set-aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the suit in the court of Assistant Judge, Badarganj, Rangpur being Other Suit No. 1032 of 2008 for declaration that the Deed No. 12809/93 dated 10-10-1993 is collusive, forged and fraudulent against the defendant-petitioner. 

 4. It is further stated that the learned Assistant Badarganj Court heard the same and by his order dated 14-9-2009 rejected the application in Other Suit No. 1032 of 2008. 

 5. It is also stated that against the afore-said order the plaintiff-opposite party filed a Civil Revisional Application before the District Judge, Rangpur being Civil Revision Case No. 42 of 2009 who heard the same and by his judgment and order dated 10-11-2001 allowed the revision and set-aside the order dated 14-9-2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Badarganj Court, in Other Suit No. 1032 of 2008. No one appears to support the Rule. 

 7. It is further contended that the learned Revisional Court committed error in law resulting error in the decision in not coming to a finding to the effect that no other deeds have been presented for the expert to compare the signature on the deed in question with the signature of the other documents under section 73 of the Evidence Act and since no document has been produced to compare the signature with the signature upon the relevant deed, as such, arrived at a wrong decision in not rejecting the applications for a hand writing expert. 

 8. The Rule has been opposed by Mr Md Abdur Rashid, the learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite parties submits that the suit being Other Suit, No. 1032 of 2008 was filed by the present opposite parties as plaintiffs for declaration that the deed No. 12809 dated 10-10-1993 as being collusive, forge and fraudulent created by the present defendant-petitioner, signatories or thumb impression containing on the said documents are to be examined by an expert in order to compare the genuine signature of the executants of the documents but the learned trial court on a misconception rejected the application by an order dated 14-9-2009. However on filing a revisional application before the district Judge, Rangpur the impugned order was passed allowing the expert to examine the signature and the thumb impression on the said documents, as such the learned appellate court below committed no error of law reversing the order of the learned trial court hence, this revisional application is liable to be discharged. 

 9. Having considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties and having perused the revisional, application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the Annexures therein, it appears that the original title suit was filed by the present opposite parties for declaring the sale deed being registered Sale Deed No. 12809 dated 10-10-1993 has been forged because the signature contained in the documents are not the signature of the genuine owners who are the present opposite parties in this revisional application. In the suit the present opposite parties filed an application under section 45 of the Evidence Act for an expert opinion of the signature and thumb impression containing in the documents which was rejected by the trial court by its order dated 14-9-2009 but the lower appellate court reversed the decision. 

 10. By virtue of the such order allowed the application filed by the present opposite parties as plaintiffs under section 45 of the Evidence Act and in order to obtain opinion as to the genuiness or legality of the documents under challenge in the original suit.  15. The interim order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule to which operation impugned judgment and order dated 10-11-2011 passed by District Judge, Rangpur, in Civil Revision No. 42 of 2009 reversing the judgment and order dated 14-9-2009 passed by Assistant Judge, Badarganj Court, Rangpur in Other Suit No. 1032 of 2003 is hereby recalled and vacated.
